title: Determiners: all, most, none, both, either
titleVi: Lượng từ: all, most, none, both, either
summary: Quy tắc of sau all/most/none, cách chia động từ với none, both/neither/either và every/each.
whyItMatters: Đây là nhóm từ bạn dùng để khái quát hoá trong Task 2: *most people*, *the majority of households*, *few governments*. Sai cấu trúc *most of people* hay *every students* là lỗi ngữ pháp cơ bản, còn dùng *all* tuyệt đối thay vì *most* lại là lỗi lập luận — cả hai đều bị trừ điểm, ở hai tiêu chí khác nhau.

sections.heading: The of-rule: all, most, some, none, no
body: These determiners go **directly before a noun** with no *of*: *all students, most people, some countries, no evidence*. They need **of** only when followed by **the, my/your/his, these/those** or an object pronoun: *all of the students, most of them, none of these countries*.
So *most people* and *most of the people* are both correct — but they mean different things. Without *of*, you generalise; with *of the*, you refer to a specific group already defined.
Object pronouns always need *of*: *all of them*, *most of us*, *none of it*. *All them* and *most us* do not exist.

rows: Most people prefer to work from home.
Most of people prefer to work from home.
Most of the people in the survey...
Most the people in the survey...
None of the evidence supports this.

sections.heading: none, no and the verb
body: **no + noun** is a determiner and makes the sentence negative on its own: *There is no evidence for this claim.* **none** stands alone as a pronoun: *None of the evidence supports this claim.*

After **none of + plural noun**, both singular and plural verbs occur. Formal writing prefers the singular: *None of the students was late.* Conversation prefers the plural: *None of the students were late.* Both are defensible; be consistent.
**none of** with an uncountable noun is always singular: *None of the information was accurate.*

examples.right: No solution has yet been found.
None of the participants was informed in advance.
examples.note: Formal register: singular verb after *none of* + plural.

examples.right: None of the data was reliable.
examples.wrong: None of the data were reliable in the singular reading.
examples.note: Với danh từ không đếm được, *none of* luôn chia số ít.

sections.heading: both, either, neither
body: **both** refers to two together and takes a plural verb: *Both options are expensive.* The correlative form is **both ... and**: *The plan is both costly and unpopular.*

**either** means one of two, **neither** means not one and not the other. Both take a **singular** verb in formal writing: *Either answer is acceptable*, *Neither proposal is affordable.* The correlatives are **either ... or** and **neither ... nor**: *Neither the government nor the council has acted.*
Position matters for *both*. It goes before the main verb but after *be* and after the first auxiliary: *They both agreed*, *We have both read it*, *They are both wrong.*

rows: Both of the reports were published.
Either the rent or the deposit has to be paid today.
Neither the students nor the teacher was satisfied.
Neither of the answers is correct.

sections.heading: every, each, all and whole
body: **every** and **each** take a **singular** noun and a singular verb: *Every candidate receives feedback*, *Each student was interviewed.* **each of** takes a plural noun but still a singular verb: *Each of the students was interviewed.*
**every** generalises over a group; **each** considers members one by one. *Every child in the country has access* (all of them, as a group) versus *Each child was given a book* (individually).

**all + plural/uncountable** versus **whole + singular countable**: *all the students*, *all the water*, *the whole class*, *the whole day*. *Whole* needs *the/my/this* before it: not *whole day*. Compare *all day* (the entire duration, no article) with *the whole day* (the same meaning, more emphatic).

examples.right: Each of the proposals has been assessed.
examples.wrong: Each of the proposals have been assessed.

examples.note: *whole* + danh từ số ít; với số nhiều dùng **all the people**.

examples.right: Every household pays a fixed fee.
examples.note: *every* + danh từ số ít, động từ số ít.

sections.heading: Hedging: why most beats all in Task 2
body: Absolute quantifiers make absolute claims, and absolute claims are easy to attack. *All governments waste money* invites a counter-example; *Most governments waste some money* is defensible and sounds more academic.

Useful hedged determiners: **most, the majority of, many, a significant proportion of, some, a minority of, few, hardly any**. Each signals a different strength of evidence, which is exactly what the Task 2 band descriptors reward under Task Response.

Pair the quantifier with a matching verb: *the majority of + plural + plural verb*, *a significant proportion of + uncountable + singular verb*. *The majority of research suggests* is a common slip — *research* is uncountable, so *the majority of the research suggests* is the precise form.

rows: The vast majority of respondents supported the ban.
Most cities face a housing shortage.
Many employers now offer hybrid work.
Some critics argue the cost is too high.
Few studies have examined this group.

commonMistakes.wrong: Most of people believe that education is free.
commonMistakes.right: Most people believe that education is free.
commonMistakes.why: Khi khái quát chung, **most + danh từ** không có *of*. Chỉ dùng *most of* khi phía sau là *the/my/these/them*: *most of the people*.

commonMistakes.wrong: All of students have to submit the form.
commonMistakes.right: All students have to submit the form. / All of the students have to submit the form.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *tất cả sinh viên* không phân biệt, nên người học chèn *of* vào giữa. Cần **all + danh từ** hoặc **all of + the + danh từ**.

commonMistakes.wrong: Every students in the class passed the test.
commonMistakes.right: Every student in the class passed the test.
commonMistakes.why: **every** và **each** luôn đi với danh từ **số ít** và động từ số ít, dù nghĩa là nhiều người.

commonMistakes.wrong: None of the participants were informed.
commonMistakes.right: None of the participants was informed.
commonMistakes.why: Trong văn viết trang trọng, **none of + số nhiều** chia động từ **số ít**. Dạng số nhiều tồn tại trong văn nói, nhưng bài thi nên chọn số ít cho nhất quán.

commonMistakes.wrong: Both of the solutions is expensive.
commonMistakes.right: Both of the solutions are expensive.
commonMistakes.why: **both** luôn mang nghĩa số nhiều nên động từ chia số nhiều, khác với *neither/either* chia số ít.

ieltsTips: Ưu tiên `most`, `the majority of`, `many` thay vì `all` — câu khẳng định tuyệt đối dễ bị phản bác và làm giảm Task Response.
Dùng `the majority of + danh từ số nhiều + động từ số nhiều`, nhưng `the majority of the research + động từ số ít`.
Trong Task 1, `most of the + danh từ xác định` dùng khi đã nêu nhóm cụ thể; `most + danh từ` dùng cho nhận định chung.
Kiểm tra vị trí `both`: sau *be* và sau trợ động từ thứ nhất — `They are both effective`, `We have both noticed`.

exercises.question: ___ of the participants was aware of the risks involved.
exercises.explanation: Có *of the* nên cần đại từ **none**: *None of the participants was...*

exercises.question: ___ households in the survey reported at least one car.
exercises.explanation: Không có *the* sau đó nên dùng **most + danh từ**: *Most households*.

exercises.question: Each of the candidates ___ a short presentation.
exercises.explanation: **each of** + danh từ số nhiều nhưng động từ **số ít**: *gives*.

exercises.question: Neither of the two proposals ___ affordable for local families.
exercises.explanation: **neither of + danh từ số nhiều** chia động từ **số ít**: *is*.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Both of the them were rejected.
exercises.explanation: **both of + đại từ tân ngữ** và động từ số nhiều.

exercises.question: ___ of the information in the report was accurate.
exercises.explanation: **None of + danh từ không đếm được** + động từ số ít.

exercises.question: ___ student in the class received individual feedback.
___ of the two proposals is financially viable.
exercises.explanation: **neither/either of + số nhiều** + động từ số ít.

exercises.question: The majority of the research ___ (suggest) a link between the two.
exercises.explanation: *research* không đếm được → động từ số ít: *suggests*.
